kaps_punt: Geen KABV-punt nie (buite KABV). Ondersteun H4 13 (onwettige mynbou en die zama-zama's).

items.bewering: Onwettige mynbou is om sonder die regering se toestemming minerale uit te haal.
items.bron: Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources media statement (gov.za, Payneville/Springs illegal gold digging): any mining without the required permits or mining rights under the MPRDA is unlawful and a criminal offence; MPRDA s5A (acts.co.za). Mining rights and permits are granted by the state (MPRDA ss 17, 23).

items.bewering: Dit gebeur dikwels in ou of verlate goudmyne
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English, 'zama zama' (dsae.co.za): informal miner working illegally, typically in disused mineshafts; Wikipedia 'Zama zama' (over 6 000 derelict and ownerless mines after the decline of gold mining); Bench Marks Foundation via EWN (abandoned mines are what attract them).

items.bewering: maar ook in myne wat nog werk en vir ander minerale
items.bron: SAnews 'Government is committed to eliminating illegal mining' (sanews.gov.za/node/59633): illegal mining now also affects operational and licensed mines; GroundUp 'Trapped between the law and zama zama gangs' (syndicates smuggle miners into operational mines by bribing employees); Wikipedia 'Zama zama' (gold, iron ore, coal, manganese); OCCRP/GI-TOC on illicit chrome mining in South Africa; SAnews/AllAfrica on unpolished diamonds confiscated in Kleinzee under Vala Umgodi.

items.bewering: Ons noem die mense wat dit doen, zama-zama's.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English, 'zama zama' (dsae.co.za/entry/zama-zama/e10061). Note for a person, not a fault: a Heinrich Böll Stiftung brief (za.boell.org, 2025) reports that many artisanal miners reject the label and that some use it only for those inside criminal syndicates. The lesson's general usage matches the dictionary.

items.bewering: In isiZulu beteken zama 'probeer', en die naam sê dus iets soos 'probeer-probeer'.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English (dsae.co.za): from isiZulu, root zama 'try, make an attempt'. Renderings of the doubled form vary ('try try', 'keep on trying', Wikipedia's 'take a chance', Böll's 'those who try their luck'); 'iets soos' hedges correctly and the repeated-trying sense is supported.

items.bewering: Baie zama-zama's kan nie werk kry nie en is baie arm. Hulle het min ander maniere om geld te verdien.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 'Blood and gold: zama zamas dice with death in daily underground hell' (13 Nov 2022): researcher Maxwell Chuma found workers had no other source of income and turned to mining because of poverty; mayor quoted calling illegal mining a response to unemployment and poverty; former mineworkers who lost jobs among them. ENACT/ISS policy brief 'Uncovered: the dark world of the Zama Zamas' (2019) likewise notes many were previously employed by mining firms.

items.bewering: Maar die werk bly onwettig en baie gevaarlik.
items.bron: DMPR statement (gov.za) on unlawfulness; Human Rights Watch figures as reported by Daily Maverick (2022): 312 informal miners dead 2012-2015 by media tally, real toll likely higher.

items.bewering: Kriminele bendes beheer dikwels hierdie werk en vat baie van die geld.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Zama zama' (miners organised by some 200 criminal syndicates); SAnews node/59633 (Minister: illegal mining is run by syndicates, miners are their foot soldiers); GroundUp 'Trapped between the law and zama zama gangs' (pyramid-shaped trade with launderers, buyers and middlemen above and miners at the bottom; armed gangs run extortion at shafts); ENACT policy brief (zama zamas organised and sustained by crime syndicates).

items.bewering: Maar die zama-zama's self loop die gevaar, en die bendes buit hulle uit.
items.bron: GroundUp (entry and exit fees of about R10 000 and R25 000, food sold at inflated prices for gold, debt bondage, some forced underground); Daily Maverick 2022 (man held at gunpoint and forced to work underground); Wikipedia 'Zama zama' (exploitative working conditions, human trafficking by syndicates).

items.bewering: Ou skagte en tonnels kan instort.
items.bron: Human Rights Watch via Daily Maverick (2022): deaths from 'collapsing tunnels, gas poisoning, suffocation and explosion accidents'; GroundUp 'Lethal toll of informal gold mining' (rock-falls a main cause of reported deaths); Creamer Media 2019 (miners mine load-bearing pillars in the seismically active Witwatersrand basin).

items.bewering: Daar is gewoonlik nie goeie ventilasie nie, en die lug kan gevaarlike gasse hê.
items.bron: GroundUp 'Trapped between the law and zama zama gangs' (the Stilfontein shaft 'is no longer ventilated'); GroundUp 'Lethal toll of informal gold mining' (carbon monoxide poisoning among main causes in 2013); HRW via Daily Maverick (gas poisoning, suffocation); Wikipedia 'Zama zama' (soldiers died of possible carbon dioxide inhalation at an illegal mine).

items.bewering: Party zama-zama's werk selfs met plofstof.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Zama zama' (rudimentary tools and explosives); Creamer Media/Mining Weekly 'Solutions beyond policing proposed as zama zamas continue to wreak havoc' (2019): uncontrolled use of explosives weakens support pillars in old mines.

items.bewering: Baie zama-zama's werk sonder die regte toerusting om veilig te bly.
items.bron: Daily Maverick 2022 ('rudimentary tools in an extreme environment'); Briefly News citing a mine safety officer at Stilfontein (no proper equipment, candles for light).

items.bewering: Daar is ook dikwels geen hulp naby vir iemand wat seerkry nie.
items.bron: Daily Maverick 2022 (injured miner waited two days underground until other zama zamas rescued him; police rarely investigate zama zama deaths); HRW (most deaths never recorded).

items.bewering: Hierdie mynbou laat oop gate en skagte agter waarin mense en diere kan val.
items.bron: Minerals Council South Africa, illegal mining page (mineralscouncil.org.za/work/illegal-mining): risk to local communities, especially children, and livestock where illegal miners break fences to reach old shafts; The Citizen/Review Online (three boys drowned in an abandoned illegal mine hole near Burgersfort; police warned that holes left open are hazardous to children); Mail & Guardian 2023 (sinkholes and road collapse from illegal digging).

items.bewering: Gif en mynafval beland ook in die water en maak dit vuil.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 'Poisoned waters: illegal mining threatens the greater Kruger ecosystem' (11 Feb 2026) and 'Spike in illegal gold mining alongside Blyde River' (17 Aug 2025): mercury and cyanide used by illegal miners, runoff and sediment reaching rivers; Mail & Guardian (lab results showing cyanide far above wildlife limits at a dam outlet); UN special rapporteur via Mail & Guardian (zama zamas still use mercury). The Department of Water and Sanitation had not yet detected cyanide or mercury at one Blyde site, but the general claim stands.

items.bewering: Die polisie tree op teen die bendes en teen onwettige mynbou.
items.bron: SAnews 'Arrests made in Vala Umgodi operations' (sanews.gov.za/node/76780) and '400 suspects arrested during nationwide Vala Umgodi operations' (node/75117): SAPS operation against illegal mining, launched late 2023.

items.bewering: Verlate skagte word toegemaak.
items.bron: PMG, parliamentary reply NW3281 (2026): the department has sealed 1 026 unsafe openings at derelict and ownerless sites since 2005; SAnews node/59633 (department seals about 40 shafts a year; Mintek sealed 135 holings in Gauteng); SAnews 'Council for Geoscience to close 45 open mine shafts'.

items.bewering: Mense in die buurt rapporteer ook waar dit gebeur.
items.bron: SAnews/AllAfrica on Vala Umgodi (public urged to report illegal mining to police stations, Crime Stop 08600 10111 or the My SAPS app); EWN, Mpumalanga MEC urging residents to report illegal miners (Aug 2025); Minerals Council anonymous tip-offs hotline (mineralscouncil.org.za/work/illegal-mining).

items.bewering: Jy moet altyd wegbly van ou mynskagte, gate en plekke waar mense myn. 'n Ou skag kan baie diep wees, en die rand kan inval.
items.bron: TimesLive/News24/Africanews on the 2017 Boksburg case (a five-year-old fell down a disused shaft about 140 m deep; ground around it caved in and was too unstable for rescuers); GroundUp (Stilfontein shaft deeper than 1.5 km); police warning near Burgersfort that open holes are hazardous to children (The Citizen).

items.bewering: onwettige mynbou: Om sonder die regering se toestemming minerale uit die grond te haal.
items.bron: DMPR statement (gov.za): mining without the permits or mining rights the MPRDA prescribes is unlawful; consistent with the study text.

items.bewering: zama-zama: Iemand wat onwettig myn, dikwels in 'n ou of verlate myn.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English: 'an informal miner who works illegally, typically in disused mineshafts'.

items.bewering: verlate myn: 'n Myn wat die eienaars agtergelaat het nadat hulle opgehou het om daar te myn.
items.bron: Yale e360 'The haunting legacy of South Africa's gold mines' and Wikipedia 'Zama zama': derelict and ownerless mines whose former owners disappeared after mining ended, leaving them the state's responsibility; Council for Geoscience programme for derelict and ownerless mines (geoscience.org.za).

items.bewering: bende: 'n Groep misdadigers wat saam onwettige dinge doen.
items.bron: Standard dictionary sense of 'bende' (a gang of criminals), as in HAT/WAT; consistent with how the sources above describe the syndicates.

items.bewering: uitbuit: Om iemand oneerlik te gebruik sodat jy voordeel uit sy werk trek.
items.bron: Standard dictionary sense of 'uitbuit' (to exploit someone, especially their labour, for your own gain), as in HAT/WAT.

items.bewering: ventilasie: Om vars lug in 'n plek in te bring, soos in 'n myn.
items.bron: Standard definition of ventilation (supplying fresh air to a space; in mining, also removing stale air and gases), e.g. HSE Blog 'Underground mining hazards'. The simplification leaves out the removal half but says nothing false.

items.bewering: plofstof: 'n Stof wat skielik met groot krag ontplof en rots kan breek.
items.bron: Standard definition of an explosive (a substance that reacts suddenly, releasing energy violently); used in mining to break rock, as with the illegal use of explosives described in Creamer Media 2019.

items.bewering: mynafval: Die rots en grond wat oorbly nadat die waardevolle mineraal of steenkool uitgehaal is.
items.bron: Standard definition of mine waste (waste rock, overburden and tailings left after the valuable material is removed), e.g. HRW 'Forever Mines' (2022) on unrehabilitated coal mine waste and Yale e360 on gold tailings. Tailings also carry processing chemicals, which the study text's 'gif en mynafval' already covers.

opsomming: Every checkable claim was confirmed against South African government, parliamentary, research and news sources, the lesson has no superlatives or analogies, and nothing in it is graphic or stigmatising (it names no nationality and does not blame the miners for the gangs' exploitation), though a person may want to know that some artisanal miners reject the name zama-zama, which the lesson uses in its general dictionary sense.
